card.title: You Owe Me a Miracle
card.instruction: Carry one past favor as sufficient reason to expect an impossible act in return, and present the exchange as perfectly fair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I covered your lunch yesterday. Bring back the ten minutes I spent queuing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That covers the sandwich. I'm only asking for my time back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can queue for you today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks. Use that time to retrieve yesterday's minutes. Then we're square.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands the lost minutes as repayment for lunch, A3 rejects replacing only the sandwich, and A5 keeps the same impossible time-debt claim.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's lunch offer gives A3 a distinction between food and time; B4's queue offer is accepted only as time to retrieve the old minutes.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 offer reasonable equivalent favors rather than refusing to repay.

heightening.evidence: A5 refers to B4's offered time but mostly repeats the initial retrieval demand without a more concrete impossible tactic.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes yesterday's lunch queue and the ten minutes A wants returned.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's then-we-are-square closes the bargain, but the use-that-time instruction is less specific than the established queue opportunity.
